description:
Why this choice is correct: NoAiaFetcher at pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:639-640 is '#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct NoAiaFetcher;'. The zero-sized unit struct is intentional. It compiles to nothing. It satisfies 'A: AiaFetcher + Default' bounds. The Copy derive is intentional even though Clone covers most uses — Copy admits pass-by-value through generic APIs that take ownership without ownership friction, which is how it will be threaded through pkix-chain::Verifier (PKIX-zkjb.9).

The companion test 'no_aia_fetcher_is_zero_sized' at line 993 pins this as a compile-time invariant. A future field addition (even PhantomData with a bound) would break the test.

A future contributor might suggest 'remove Copy, Clone is sufficient'. Reject: Copy is the ergonomic difference that makes pass-by-value through generic Verifier construction painless. The ZST means there is literally nothing to clone or move; Copy reflects that fact at the type-system level.

A future contributor might also suggest 'replace this with () or PhantomData and have impl AiaFetcher for ()'. Reject: a named type carries documentation and is greppable. () impls cannot carry rustdoc. NoAiaFetcher is the API; the ZST is the implementation.
title: Decision: NoAiaFetcher is ZST with Copy + Default + zero allocation
